answer: Hardware remote attestation resists Sybil attacks for agent networks managing river logistics or onyx trades. During onboarding, each agent binds a session cipher key inside a hardware enclave and submits a vendor-signed attestation quote that peers verify against a root key. Faking identities forces an attacker to acquire distinct physical chips, incurring real silicon procurement costs. However, leaked vendor keys or rented cloud enclaves can still enable cheap multi-instance spoofing.
